revisions.summary: Nothing changed in the reading: it is the one approved before the blend took its place as the main reading.

The intention: Let the opening F hang, then gather speed under the singer until the drums take over. The last three drum steps send the rider up into the bright stab at twelve seconds. The bass catches him and sends him skimming through the hook. He gives up speed for the lower singer, takes off again with the roll and coasts out on the drums.

The intention: Let the opening F hang on a light catch, then gather speed under the singer as the drums come in. The climb stays low until the last drum gives way to one high arc into the bright stab. The bass hook skips forward close to the line, while the low singer gets a slower, rounder answer. Light syllables leave more room around the accents. The roll tightens low and fast, then the drums get the last lift.

The intention: The singer alone at the start is weightless: the rider floats slowly, long in the air, every catch a whisper. When the drums arrive it comes down to earth, and the climb lifts each arc a little higher than the last, until the long breath before the stab throws it into the biggest loft of the song. From the stab on, with the bass under it, it runs low and fast, close to the line, and the body's strokes fall into a few clear weights instead of many near-equal ones. The lower singer lifts it off the ground again, slower and rounder, before the full drums send it flat and fast to the last four strokes. The approved reading changed height and pace only gradually across the song; here the two singers float and the bass runs. Most visible at the stab (12.2 s) and when the lower voice takes over (26.9 s).

The intention: Two singers float, the bass runs, and every big entrance arrives at full pace. The upper singer at the start is light and slow, long in the air, as all three new readings had it, on the approved catches made a little softer (Astra). The drums bring the rider down; the climb stays low and fast and keeps all its lift for one high arc into the bright stab, the arc that came out highest in Sol's ride. Under the bass it runs close to the line on the approved strengths, rising only where the hook leaves its two longest breaths (Sol). The lower singer floats again, slower and rounder, as the new readings had it. My own part: that float gathers pace over its last bar, so the full drums at 34.8 land with the weight the approved ride gave them and the new readings lost; the approved handoff keeps its strong stroke, and the last two drum steps lift away into the loop.
This is the blend, the main reading of the song since 2026-11-19. Nothing changed in it.
